ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a horizontally relatively long rectangle. There is one point at each of the midpoints of the upper side and the lower side, and slanted lines connect from these midpoints to the four opposite vertices, forming a gray shaded rhombus in the middle. The upper and lower vertices of the gray rhombus are respectively the midpoints of the upper side and lower side of the rectangle, and the left and right vertices are the intersection points of the two groups of slanted lines. Reasoning: Let the rectangle have width W and height H, take the lower-left corner as (0,0), the lower-right corner as (W,0), the upper-left corner as (0,H), and the upper-right corner as (W,H). The midpoint of the lower side is B=(W/2,0), and the midpoint of the upper side is T=(W/2,H). The left intersection point is obtained from the intersection of the line from T to the lower-left corner and the line from B to the upper-left corner. The line from T to the lower-left corner is y=(2H/W)x, and the line from B to the upper-left corner is y=H-(2H/W)x; their intersection gives x=W/4, y=H/2. Similarly, the right intersection point is (3W/4,H/2). Therefore the vertical diagonal length of the shaded rhombus is H, and the horizontal diagonal length is W/2. The area of the rhombus is (1/2)·H·(W/2)=WH/4. The area of the rectangle is WH, so the proportion of the shaded part occupying the rectangle is (WH/4)/WH=1/4.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/diagonal-area route. From the image, identify a wide rectangle with the top and bottom side midpoints joined by slanted segments to the four opposite vertices, producing a shaded central diamond whose top and bottom vertices are the two midpoints. Let the rectangle have width W and height H, with bottom-left (0,0), bottom-right (W,0), top-left (0,H), top-right (W,H). The midpoints are B=(W/2,0) and T=(W/2,H). Use the two left slanted lines T to bottom-left and B to top-left; their intersection is (W/4,H/2). Similarly, the right intersection is (3W/4,H/2). Thus the shaded diamond has vertical diagonal H and horizontal diagonal W/2, so its area is (1/2)(H)(W/2)=WH/4. Divide by the rectangle area WH to get 1/4.

method.method_draft: Equal-area dissection route. From the image, see that the vertical segment between the two side midpoints divides the rectangle into two congruent half-rectangles. In the left half-rectangle, the two drawn slanted segments are exactly its diagonals: top-left to bottom-midpoint and bottom-left to top-midpoint. Diagonals of a rectangle intersect at the center and split that half-rectangle into four equal-area triangles. The same happens in the right half-rectangle. Therefore the whole rectangle is divided into 8 equal-area triangular pieces. The shaded diamond is made of the two triangles adjacent to the central vertical midpoint segment, one in each half-rectangle. Hence the shaded fraction is 2/8=1/4.
